title: Starlane - Legal & Security: Prompt Ephemerality and Data Handling Review
summary: Review focused on prompt/content retention policy, PII/PHI handling, contractual 'no training' commitments, and technical controls (KMS/BYOK, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, data residency). Redwood team clarified hosted vs Dedicated/Private behaviors, described ephemeral cache patterns and retention windows, and agreed to follow up with a tailored security addendum and benchmark access for the infra team.
topics: encryption at rest and in transit / KMS
data residency and private deployment options
contractual security addendum and SOC2 evidence

Liam to receive invited access to a staging Dedicated node for a short throughput test (coordinate dates)
Priya and Redwood legal to sync on no-train clause language; schedule follow-up week of 2025-12-22

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-15 13:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Olivia Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Bell (Redwood SE), Nadia Chopra (CISO, Starlane), Ethan Ruiz (Head of ML), Priya Kapoor (Counsel), Liam Zhang (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy): quick run through of security posture, clarifying prompt retention and whether data is used for model training, talk through KMS and audit logs.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Olivia): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we know this is a cross-functional readout — legal, infra, sec — so appreciate you making time. quick agenda; walk through the no-train position, how prompts are handled in hosted vs dedicated/private, and then answer any legal questions.

00:28 Speaker 2 (Nadia): thanks Olivia. quick context — Starlane is moving to prod in Q1, and security needs to confirm we can meet no-train commitments for PII/PHI and provide audit trails. we'll also want clear TTLs on prompt storage.

00:46 Speaker 1 (Olivia): absolutely. to start high level: by default Redwood's hosted API does not use customer prompt or response data to further train public models. we also offer contractual "no-train" language and dedicated/private deployments where customer data stays in your VPC. caveat — i'll let Marcus dig into the runtime specifics.

01:12 Speaker 3 (Marcus): yep, thanks. so there are three patterns: hosted (multi-tenant control plane, isolated per-tenant data stores and opt-out for training), dedicated (reserved GPU pools, data scoped to your capacity) and private (full control plane in your VPC or on-prem). for hosted we have an opt-out flag and don't feed customer prompts into our model training pipelines. some customers want BYOK for keys — we support KMS integrations and HSM in Private.

01:50 Nadia: when you say "don't feed into model training" — is that a policy or a technical block? we need both: contractual and demonstrable technical controls.

02:07 Marcus: fair question — there are two levers. policy/contractually, we provide the addendum that says Redwood won't train models on Customer Data. tech-wise, the training pipelines ingest only curated datasets; there are filters and access controls preventing customer-synced buckets from being included. for hosted we isolate logs and we have TTLs; ephemeral caches and KV caches are rotated.

02:45 Priya: what are the actual TTLs? are prompts persisted for 30 days, 90 days, indefinitely? what's default?

03:02 Marcus: default for hosted telemetry is 30 days, but prompts used for debugging are stored in an encrypted store with a 30-day retention unless you request a shorter window. for Dedicated the default is retention until you configure otherwise — but we can set retention policy to zero (ephemeral) if you want. note: full audit logs (access traces) are typically 90 days in hosted; we can extend with add-on.

03:35 Ethan: i know other vendors say "no training" but then have opt-ins; can you confirm we won't see any derivative model drift because of our data?

03:50 Marcus: we can't guarantee downstream third-party models' behavior, but on Redwood's internal pipelines — customer data is never placed into training corpora unless there's an explicit opt-in and legal agreement. i realize that's generic wording; the addendum will be specific. also for customers that need absolute segregation we recommend Dedicated or Private.

04:22 Liam: on the KMS side — can we use our AWS KMS key for encrypting request payloads at rest, or do you only support server-side keys?

04:36 Marcus: hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS (BYOK) for data-at-rest encryption for some artifacts; Private supports HSM. we do envelope encryption: your CMK wraps our data encryption keys. note there are limited API paths where BYOK is supported today; we'll send the matrix.

05:05 Nadia: audit logs — we need immutable traces for access to prompts and responses; names of users, API keys used, and IP addresses. does Redwood persist that and can we export them?

05:25 Marcus: yes, audit logs include actor, action, resource, timestamp, and source IP. hosted gives you the logs and you can stream to your SIEM (cloudwatch/stackdriver/third-party) via a logs export; Dedicated can write directly to your log collector. exports are near real-time.

05:52 Priya: related to PII/PHI — we need to know if there's any NLP-derived outputs that might inadvertently leak PHI; how do you flag or redact? any DLP built-in?

06:10 Marcus: we have built-in pattern matching rules and a DLP pipeline that can be enabled — it scans prompt text and can mask common PII (SSNs, credit cards, etc.). for PHI it's more contextual; we recommend customer-side pre-processing / client-side redaction or a server-side pre-ingest DLP step. we'll send the DLP ruleset and limitations.

06:38 Ethan: practically, if our product sends PHI accidentally, can Redwood guarantee it won't be used in training and that it will be deleted immediately?

06:51 Olivia: contractually we can agree to immediate deletion requests and a no-train clause; operationally, we have support paths to purge data and we log purges. Marcus will detail the purge window.

07:06 Marcus: purge requests hit our ingestion store and then remove the record from the short-term cache and encrypted storage. retention indexes are updated; there's an eventual consistency window — typically a background job that completes within 24 hours, metadata removed within 72 hours in hosted. for Dedicated / Private purge is under your admin control.

07:36 Nadia: 24 to 72 hours is a bit wide for us. can you reduce that SLA for the contract?

07:46 Olivia: we can discuss a contractual SLA for purge completion; we'll need legal to sign off and Marcus to confirm the typical operational range and failure modes.

08:05 Priya: we will likely request a data residency clause — some of our customers are EU and cannot cross borders. can Redwood guarantee EU-only storage for prompt data?

08:22 Marcus: yes — we can pin data to regions; for hosted we run regionally isolated storage in eu-west-1, us-east-1, etc. Dedicated lets you pick the region for your cluster. Private gives you full control.

08:44 Liam: on RBAC — we need fine-grained roles; we don't want devs to see production prompts. can you show how roles map to console/SDK/API access?

09:00 Marcus: RBAC is at the org, project, and route level. roles are Admin, Developer, Ops, ReadOnly; you can scope tokens to routes. we also support SSO via SAML/Okta and SCIM provisioning. for the API we issue scoped API keys with limited permissions. we'll attach the role matrix.

09:29 Ethan: would Redwood consider attribute-based access for certain consumers — like data-mapped tokens?

09:36 Marcus: we have a roadmap for more granular attribute-based auth. right now scoping tokens to routes and projects is the practical control; can discuss timelines if that's a hard blocker.

09:52 Nadia: one worry — transcripts and recordings of audio or meeting notes, if sent to the API, are they treated differently? i.e., are audio transcripts considered PII?

10:08 Marcus: content is content — we treat text the same as other payloads. we do have specialized controls in Private deployments for audio artifacts. best practice is client-side redaction before callouts.

10:32 Priya: regarding evidence — can we get your SOC 2 Type II report and ISO certs? and do you have third-party pen test reports?

10:43 Olivia: yes, we'll share a redacted SOC 2 report and ISO attestations. pen test summaries are available; details are under NDA typically. we'll include links in the addendum.

11:00 Ethan: earlier you mentioned KV cache and prefix caching being ephemeral — can you explain the default behavior? does the KV cache persist across sessions or is it per-request?

11:18 Marcus: KV cache is a runtime optimization; for hosted it's per-model-session and TTL-based. it helps reduce repeated compute for long conversations but is not a training corpus. for strict privacy you can disable caching at the request level or request a zero-TTL retention for your account.

11:46 Nadia: nice. i want to call out that our compliance team will want a diagram of data flows — where prompts touch Redwood systems, what are the storage layers, contact points, and who has keys. can you produce that?

12:05 Olivia: yes, we'll produce a data flow diagram and include where KMS lives, which logs are exported, and typical retention.

12:18 Priya: and the contract — we will push back on any ambiguous "we may" language around training and retention. we need absolute language.

12:31 Olivia: understood. Redwood's legal is used to these asks; we'll propose firm language and also a cut of technical controls in the addendum.

12:42 Liam: for the staging Dedicated node test — can we run a throughput run and validate that logs show the right metadata and that BYOK works?

12:55 Marcus: yes, we'll provision a staging Dedicated instance and provide temporary keys and access for Liam's team. we'll coordinate timing offline.

13:10 Ethan: two small items — can you expose an endpoint or callback for immediate purge confirmation and a webhook for deletion events?

13:21 Marcus: webhook for deletions is on the integration roadmap; currently we return synchronous delete confirmations and backend jobs update the index. we can add webhook as a prioritized item for Dedicated customers.

13:38 Priya: what's the escalation path if we suspect a data leak? we need an incident response playbook and PII notification timeline.

13:48 Olivia: incident response is handled by our security team; we'll share the incident response playbook and standard notification SLA (we typically notify customers within 24 hours of detection for confirmed incidents). exact timelines can be contractually adjusted for enterprise deals.

14:05 Nadia: ok, this helps. any gotchas or limitations we should know about?

14:14 Marcus: a couple: BYOK support has a limited matrix for certain artifacts; immediate purge has an eventual consistency window; some audit log retention beyond 90 days is an add-on; DLP has pattern-based limits and may not catch complex PHI without tuning. we'll spell this out in the tech note.

14:36 Olivia: to wrap, quick recap: Redwood confirms contractual no-train options and technical controls, we'll send SOC2 and addendum, Marcus will provide the ephemeral cache/TTL tech note and a mapping of BYOK capabilities, and we'll provision a staging Dedicated environment for Liam and Ethan to test.

14:56 Nadia: thanks — please send the docs. Priya will follow up with specific legal language.

15:06 Olivia: thanks all. we'll follow up with the links and schedule the legal sync.

15:15 (call end)

Notes on transcription quirks: occasional mis-hearings ("SOC two" sometimes transcribed as "sock two"), speaker attribution has a couple generic "Speaker 1" lines; timestamps approximate.
